newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Ex-racing driver to run for Argentine presidency.
newsitem.headline: Ex-racing driver to run for Argentine presidency.

text.p: Former Formula One racing driver Carlos Reutemann has announced he is preparing to run for president of Argentina as a Peronist Party candidate to succeed Carlos Menem.
"On Sunday, I telephoned President Carlos Menem, and he gave me his total support," Reutemann said late Monday.

Reutemann said he would formally announce his candidacy on Thursday. He has been a senator since completing a term as governor of Santa Fe province, where he was handpicked as the local Peronist candidate by Menem.
The former Formula One world championship runner-up will compete against two other Peronists in the race to succeed Menem, who must step down after his second term in office ends in 1999.

The front-runner so far has been the powerful governor of Buenos Aires province, Eduardo Duhalde. Another celebrity-turned-governor, Ramon Ortega, a former pop singer who led the Tucuman provincial government, is also running.
The tall, craggy-faced Reutemann told local radio that Buenos Aires taxi drivers had helped convince him to run for president.
"Over the past year-and-a-half I have taken approximately 1,500 taxis and they all tell me 'Why don't you have a go? You're a serious sort of guy and the country needs you'," Reutemann said.
The Peronist Party was founded as a populist movement by Gen. Juan Peron in the 1940s.
But Menem has presided over austere economic reforms which have shrivelled inflation and boosted Argentina's economic competitiveness but at the cost of 17.3 percent unemployment.
